clue.text: Retired bishop enrolled in beginner's course

indicators.note: being enrolled puts the bishop's letter inside the turned-round word
something retired has gone back, so the word for a beginner is read backwards

parts.note: a tiro is a beginner or novice
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop in retirement signs up for a course for beginners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns TIRO into ORIT, and 'enrolled in' puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is the regular path or track a planet follows, a synonym for course.

clue.text: Set up orgies and capers

indicators.note: capers are frolics or antics, so the letters before it are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone arranges orgies and wild pranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capers' rearranges the letters of ORGIES AND.
explanation.definitionFit: To be set up is to be arranged in order, a synonym for organised.

clue.text: Delight when trap is set up before long

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means raised, so the word for a trap is read bottom to top

parts.note: a web is a spider's trap
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: Joy comes once a snare is laid ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To delight someone is to charm or enchant them, which is what bewitching means.

clue.text: Coach tour omits university, previously featured centrally

indicators.note: previously places the central letters ahead of the shortened tour
only the central letters of the word featured are used
the word tour leaves out the letter for university

explanation.surface: A coach trip leaves out the university that it had featured earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centrally' takes TU from the middle of fEATURed's eight letters; 'omits' takes U out of TOUR to leave TOR; 'previously' puts TU first.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a private teacher who prepares a student, a synonym for tutor.

clue.text: Typewriter device restricted in due course, so they say

indicators.note: so they say signals that the words are heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: restricted means taboo and in due course means later, said together

explanation.surface: A part of a typewriter that will be banned eventually, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: TABOO LATER, spoken aloud, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabulator is the key on a typewriter that jumps to set column positions.

clue.text: Thief, very young, caught in playground, climbing

parts.note: a child aged two is very young
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads the playground word from bottom to top

parts.note: REC, short for recreation ground, is a British playground

explanation.surface: A very young thief is caught in the playground while climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns REC into CER. A TWOCCER is British slang for a car thief, from TWOC, taking without owner's consent.
explanation.definitionFit: A twoccer is a British slang term for a joyrider who steals cars, so a kind of thief.

clue.text: Caustic name for flier

parts.note: a caustic remark is bitter

explanation.surface: A sharp remark serves as the name for some airman.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a marsh bird of the heron family, so a flier.

clue.text: Clint goes for "fifty times one" with time running down

indicators.note: in a down clue the time letter moves further down the word

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Clint Eastwood is cast as 'fifty times one' as the clock ticks down.
explanation.walkthrough: L TIMES ONE has its T moved further down, giving L IMES T ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A clint is a block of rock in a limestone pavement, so the word can stand for that rock.

clue.text: Minister repeatedly concealing limits of service

indicators.note: concealing means the answer is tucked inside the doubled word, so the letters around it are dropped
the word minister is written twice in a row

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A minister keeps hiding the limits of the service he offers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' writes MINISTER MINISTER; the answer sits across the join, so the outer MINIS and STER fall away.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are the end stations of a train or bus route, the limits of a service.

clue.text: Verse of song cut short — put in a note

indicators.note: the shortened song is put inside the note

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the word for song is removed

parts.note: a hymn is a religious song

explanation.surface: A verse of a song, abridged, is inserted in a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the N from HYMN, and HYM goes 'in' RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyme is a name for verse or poetry, as in 'nursery rhyme'.

clue.text: Two I ought to change or give up

indicators.note: change means the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A two-way choice: change your ways or quit.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something up is to do without it, an idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: Doctor attending fish — an eel

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A doctor treating a fish learns it is an eel.
explanation.definitionFit: The moray is a tropical eel with sharp teeth, a species of that fish.

clue.text: At cricket, run Sue out — score?

indicators.note: out means the letters of the words before it are disordered

explanation.surface: At a cricket match, a run-out of a player called Sue: what is the score?
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges AT CRICKET RUN SUE. 'Score' wants to mean runs; here it is a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's ballet suite is a musical score, signalled by the question mark as an example.

clue.text: Student and companion accommodated in upper room of old house

indicators.note: the companion's letters are lodged inside the room word

parts.note: a solar was the upper living room in a medieval house
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A student and a friend are put up in the top room of an ancient mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, for Companion of Honour, a British honour, is 'accommodated in' SOLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a student, especially one holding a scholarship.

clue.text: Left one variety of 5 in waste disposal unit

parts.note: the Roman numeral one is I

indicators.note: a variety of the bird's name is a rearrangement of its letters

parts.note: 5 refers to the answer at 5 down, the marsh bird

explanation.surface: One type of marsh bird was left in the rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges BITTERN, the answer to 5 down, into TTERBIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter bin is a container for rubbish in a public place.

clue.text: Implement repositioning of hotline

indicators.note: the letters of hotline are moved into new positions

explanation.surface: An instruction to rearrange a direct phone line.
explanation.definitionFit: A neolith is a stone tool or implement from the New Stone Age.

clue.text: Harassed bird took a little food

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
to peck is to eat small bits of food

explanation.surface: A harried bird had a nibble.
explanation.definitionFit: Henpecked means nagged or harassed, typically by a domineering partner.

clue.text: Severe setback for club, perhaps, after it's infiltrated

indicators.note: a setback is a backward turn, so the whole construction is read in reverse
the club word is infiltrated by the letters of it's

parts.note: a club is one example of a playing card

explanation.surface: A club suffers a bad setback after it has been infiltrated.
explanation.walkthrough: ITS 'infiltrated' into CARD gives CITSARD, and 'setback' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are severe or extreme ones.

clue.text: Saxifrage, short flower, about one pound

indicators.note: about means the shortened flower goes round the other letters
short means the final letter of the flower word is lost

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower
the Roman numeral one is I
LB is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: A saxifrage, a small flower weighing roughly a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' takes R from ASTER, and ASTE goes 'about' I and LB.
explanation.definitionFit: The astilbe is a perennial plant of the saxifrage family.

clue.text: Sabotage beginning to cause waves

indicators.note: only the first letter of cause is used

parts.note: to ripple is to form small waves

explanation.surface: An act of sabotage starts to send ripples out.
explanation.definitionFit: To cripple a plan or machine is to disable it, as sabotage does.

clue.text: Interrupt burglary

definitions.meaning: an illegal entry into a building

explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms of the phrasal verb: cutting into talk is a verb sense, and a forced entry by thieves is the noun sense.

clue.text: Exercising is not good for sportswear

indicators.note: not means the letter for good is taken away

parts.note: biking, riding a bicycle, is a form of exercising

explanation.surface: Doing exercise isn't good for athletic clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikinis are two-piece swimsuits, worn for beach sport and so a kind of sportswear.

clue.text: Sticking unpleasant character up in Greece's capital

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for a nasty person is read upward

parts.note: a fink is a contemptible person or informer

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of Greece

explanation.surface: Stabbing a nasty person in the Greek capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FINK into KNIF; Greece's 'capital' is G.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticking someone means stabbing them, which is knifing.

clue.text: Locked up frequently, I am finally free — at the critical moment

parts.note: in the nick is British slang for in prison
oft is a poetic word for often

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of each of the words I, am and free

explanation.surface: Often locked up, a prisoner at last goes free just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: THE NICK is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Just in time, at the last possible moment, is the idiomatic meaning.

clue.text: Newton giving two different accounts

parts.note: an ISA is an Individual Savings Account, a British tax-free savings account
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A Newton who tells two different stories.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a British tax-free savings account.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Isaac Newton, the physicist, is identified by his first name.

clue.text: It's criminal to use offensive weapons

definitions.meaning: a receiver who buys and sells stolen goods
to fight with swords as a sport

explanation.definitionFit: A fence is a dealer in stolen goods; to fence is to fight with swords.

clue.text: First of actors delivered lines in Ben- Hur without any preparation

indicators.note: the first letter of each word from actors to Ben-Hur is taken

explanation.surface: The actors in Ben-Hur spoke their lines without rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of' applies to all five words: A, D, L, I, B.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak ad lib is to improvise, speaking without preparation.

clue.text: Kind of drawing, showing necessities for calligraphy

definitions.meaning: a sketch made with a nib and liquid colour
the tools needed for handwriting art

explanation.definitionFit: A pen-and-ink sketch is a drawing style, and a pen and ink are the tools of calligraphy.

clue.text: Purity originally connected with being thin

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of connected

parts.note: leanness is the state of being thin

explanation.surface: Purity first linked with slimness.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleanness is the state of being clean, a synonym for purity.

clue.text: Stole with decorative border

definitions.meaning: crept stealthily, as in stole away

explanation.definitionFit: Edged can mean moved gradually, like stole, or having a border.
